findings.ref: human-copy/plugins/sdd-quality-loop/scripts/resolve-project-context.py: class AffectedComponentResolutionFailed / _run_resolve_component_paths OSError branch / main() step 4 handler
findings.note: The step-4 launch-failure path emits a malformed, non-canonical diagnostic. `except OSError as exc: raise AffectedComponentResolutionFailed(f'launch failed: {exc}')` binds that string to `self.returncode` (the constructor's only parameter), and main() interpolates it into design.md's fixed M8 sentence, producing `capability-resolver: affected-component-resolution-failed: resolve-component-paths exited launch failed: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: <abs path> resolving ...`. That breaks AC-014/M8 (canonical, Resolver-owned detail, never raw upstream text), breaks REQ-005 byte-identical dual-runtime parity (the OSError text is platform/locale dependent), and writes an absolute filesystem path into the git-committed Resolver Evidence that security-spec classifies as carrying ids/digests/evidence only. Reachable whenever _script_argv falls through to the bare `resolve-component-paths` name. No fixture covers it: the only fixture stub exits 3, exercising the well-formed exit-code branch.

API/Contract Plan step 8 (matched-Capability conditional-facet evaluation), which this task owns, has zero executed coverage. Every fixture Registry in the bundle declares conditional_facets: [] (dsl-warn-matched-nondetermining, dsl-warn-unmatched-trigger, registry-validation-failed) or zero capabilities (dependency-subprocess-failed, capability-registry-empty.json used by both projection success fixtures), so the `if matched:` branch of _evaluate_capabilities never runs in any of the 102 assertions. B7 declaration_index keying, the facet-level union `applied` rule, the per-component facet fan-out, and B2's widened WARN detection inside conditional_facet_evaluations[].evaluations[] are all implemented but never exercised; the only evidence is the hard-coded conditional_facet_evaluations: [] the test itself expects.

findings.ref: resolve-project-context.py: _evaluate_capabilities() component loop (for component_id in affected_components)
findings.note: REQ-005's determinism obligation cited in this task's own Requirements line ('ascending-lexicographic per-component fan-out') and design.md step 7 ('for each affected_components[] entry in ascending lexicographic order') is not implemented and not tested. The code iterates the array in whatever order resolve-component-paths returned, with only a source comment ('already returned pre-sorted') standing in for the guarantee; nothing in the bundle establishes that upstream ordering contract, and no fixture exercises an unsorted upstream list (the sole multi-component fixture has exactly two ids already in lexicographic order). Since trigger_evaluations[] order is derived from this loop, an unsorted upstream silently produces non-deterministic Evidence.

findings.ref: resolve-project-context.py: _discover_registry() / _generate_registry_digest_whole(); design.md Data Plan 'Invocation-start snapshot ... (B8)' and API/Contract Plan steps 5-6
findings.note: Spec drift on the B8 Registry snapshot. Design requires the invocation to retain the located Registry's canonicalized bytes in memory and 'never re-read any of the three paths from disk again except for the two rechecks', and step 6 to run generate-registry-digest --whole against the located Registry. The implementation keeps only a parsed dict from step 5 and invokes generate-registry-digest --whole with no registry argument, so the digest is computed from an independent second ADR-0025 discovery and disk read (the docstring admits this). A Registry edit between step 5 and step 6 yields a registry_digest that does not bind the bytes steps 7-8 actually evaluated, and the step-13 recheck compares against that already-drifted value. No fixture covers the divergence.

An affected component absent from the Context Projection is silently evaluated against empty properties rather than surfaced. Under the governing 'ambiguous means Block' rule and this task's own Risk Rationale (silent under-match is the named hazard), a Projection/affected-component mismatch degrading to a probable false with no diagnostic is a silent-degradation path. No diagnostic id is assigned and no fixture exercises it.

Two evidence-narrative inaccuracies. traceability.log cites 'CASE_NAMES list (line 160-165)' as enumerating the six T-003 fixtures, but the driver defines no CASE_NAMES identifier at all (T-002's tuple is CASES; the six names sit at the tail of ALL_CASE_NAMES). The contract comment still asserts 'HONEST FINDING ... task-state-check is recorded below as passes:false/required:true, which will itself make check-contract report this contract FAILED' while the check block records passes: true; only an appended sentence reconciles it, leaving the contract's own narrative self-contradictory.

The expectation is tautological with respect to the property the fixture is named for: expected_capability_evaluations uses 'matched': result and 'result': result, where result comes from the real evaluate-predicate. Nothing asserts result is False, so the fixture would still pass if the predicate began matching and the 'unmatched Capability trigger WARN' half of B2's widened quantifier silently stopped being exercised.

Neither suite twin is included, so the only evidence for the acceptance-tests check (focused-tests-ps1.log) cannot be tied to an actual PowerShell dispatcher invocation: the shared Python driver prints runtime-independent labels, and the ps1 log is byte-equivalent to the sh log. Relatedly, the implementation report's Done-When self-check claims those two files 'gain this task's own six new fixtures' while its own git-derived Outputs table lists neither, which the identical PASS labels in both logs make plausible but the bundle cannot confirm.
